Shiny lets you turn R code into an **interactive web application**: the user clicks, chooses and uploads, and R does the computations behind the scenes.

In this course we start from an empty RStudio project and finish with **your own app online**, with a link you can send to anyone.

## The plan

### Day 1 · The logic of Shiny

| Topic | What you take home |
|---|---|
| [Shiny](day1/00-shiny.qmd) | What Shiny is and the logic behind it: UI, server and their communication |
| [A Shiny project](day1/01-project.qmd) | An RStudio project with `ui.R` and `server.R` that runs |
| [How Shiny thinks](day1/02-logic.qmd) | Inside the UI and the server: IDs and reactivity |
| [Input widgets](day1/03-inputs.qmd) | What each widget sends to the server |
| [Outputs and render functions](day1/04-outputs.qmd) | How results go back to the UI |
| [Reactivity and `reactive()`](day1/05-reactive.qmd) | When the server re-runs your code |
| [Wait for it: `eventReactive()`](day1/06-eventreactive.qmd) | Deciding *when* the app reacts |
| [Your app: explore a dataset](day1/07-explore.qmd) | A complete app, built step by step |

### Day 2 · Spread the shine

| Topic | What you take home |
|---|---|
| [Your app on GitHub](day2/08-github.qmd) | The project in a GitHub repository |
| [Deploy on Connect Cloud](day2/09-deploy.qmd) | Your app online |

[Going further](extras/index.qmd) collects the topics we will not cover in class (layouts, updating inputs, interactive plots, downloads), with working apps you can study on your own.

## Before the course

::: {.callout-important}
## Please do this **before** Day 1

1. Install [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) and [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) (recent versions)
2. Install the packages we need:

    ```r
    install.packages(c("shiny", "rsconnect"))
    ```

3. Create a free [GitHub](https://github.com/) account and install [GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com/)
4. Create a free account on [Posit Connect Cloud](https://connect.posit.cloud/), signing in **with your GitHub account**
:::

## How to use these pages

Most examples are **live apps that run in your browser**. Each app is shown twice:

1. **first the app alone**: play with it and see what it does
2. **then its code** (`ui.R` and `server.R` in two tabs), with the explanation and the same app running below it

- You can **edit the code** and re-run the app with the ▶ button (or {{< kbd Ctrl-Shift-Enter >}})
- Nothing you do here can break anything: reload the page to start over
- The first app on a page takes a few seconds to start (R is being loaded in your browser)

::: {.callout-tip}
## All the apps, ready to run

All the apps of the course are in the [`apps`](https://github.com/ottaviae/stat-shiny/tree/main/apps) folder of the repository. Each app is a folder with a `ui.R` and a `server.R` file.

[Download all the apps (.zip)](apps.zip){.btn .btn-primary}
:::
